source.title: What Dyadic Reparation Is Meant to Do: An Association with Infant Cortisol Reactivity.

confidence_rationale: First empirical demonstration that interactive repair (latency to reparation of dyadic mismatches in the Face-to-Face Still-Face paradigm) is associated with infant psychobiological stress reactivity (cortisol), independent of maternal diagnostic category -- 'infants respond to what they experience and not to the maternal diagnostic category.' Grounds the core of the rupture-and-repair model that INV-082's safe base and LOVE-4/LOVE-5 stand on: rupture is normal and recurrent, and it is the REPAIR that regulates the infant. Held below 0.7 by small sample (46 dyads, 16 imputed cortisol values), correlational design, and the large gap from infant HPA-axis regulation to a computational self-valence channel.
failure_signatures: Small sample (n=46) with 16 imputed cortisol values and a correlational design -- the repair/cortisol association is real but the effect's robustness and direction of causation are not nailed down.

The study measures physiological stress regulation (cortisol reactivity), not the self-valence or rule-update outcomes INV-082/LOVE-4 actually care about; it grounds 'repair regulates the infant' but not the specific 'correction updates rule/harm models without self-valence collapse' separation.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In the Face-to-Face Still-Face paradigm, the latency to interactive repair of dyadic mismatches during the reunion episode is associated with infant cortisol reactivity; the association holds regardless of maternal anxiety-disorder status. Interactive repair, not the absence of rupture, is what relates to the infant's psychobiological stress regulation.
mapping.ree_translation: The rupture-and-repair model underwrites INV-082's safe base and the LOVE-4/LOVE-5 mechanisms: relationships are not rupture-free; what makes correction survivable is the presence of a reliable REPAIR loop after the mismatch. This paper is the empirical anchor that repair is the regulating event (it is 'what dyadic reparation is meant to do'), grounding LOVE-5 love-mediated-repair as relationship restoration that down-regulates distress -- the constructive counterpart to the punishment-avoidance / appeasement failure modes. The 'infants respond to what they experience' finding maps onto the project rule that the agent must learn from the actual correction/repair dynamics, not a label.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Infant-caregiver dyadic physiology (cortisol) is several steps removed from REE's correction/repair machinery; the study measures stress regulation, not the rule/harm-model update or self-valence stability that LOVE-4/LOVE-5 instrument. It supports the GENERAL rupture-repair frame strongly and the SPECIFIC self-valence-preservation claim only by extension. Correlational; small imputed-data sample.
mapping.source_context: 46 mother-infant dyads (19 maternal anxiety disorder, 27 control), Face-to-Face Still-Face paradigm at 3-4 months postpartum; salivary cortisol reactivity; Tronick a co-author.

confidence_components.notes: Modest sample with imputed cortisol values caps source quality, but it is a landmark first demonstration of the repair/physiology link from the Tronick group. Mapping fidelity moderate: strong for the rupture-repair frame, weaker for the specific self-valence-preservation mechanism. Transfer risk substantial (infant HPA axis -> computational self-valence).
